newsitem.title: USA: Biovail shorts may face surprise -- report.
newsitem.headline: Biovail shorts may face surprise -- report.

text.p: Shortsellers of Biovail Corp International's stock could be unpleasantly surprised if the company fulfills its growth potential, Barron's financial weekly said.

The newspaper said the company had a 62.5 percent increase in short sales of its stock in the four weeks ended August 15, bringing the total short position to three million of its 25.4 million shares outstanding.

Barron's said the main arguments against the company involve a recent discounted stock sale to George Soros and other investors, worries regarding wholesale demand for the hypertension drug Tiazac, and concerns about Biovail's ability to apply its time-release technology to other drugs.
However, Biovail's chairman Eugene Melnyk said he is "very comfortable" with analysts' earnings estimates of $0.90 a share this year and about $1.50 next year, Barron's said.

Melnyk also said Biovail expects to announce by the end of this year an agreement with an undisclosed drug company to sell a generic form of Procardia XL, Pfizer Inc's hypertension drug, Barron's reported.
A managing partner at Oracle Partners, one of the firms that bought into Biovail along with Soros last May, said he was initially skeptical about the company.

"But I have high confidence now that Biovail's answer to Procardia XL works, and I wouldn't want to be short this stock. We're in it for the home-run potential," Oracle's Larry Feinberg told the paper.
